::: {#sol-square-three}

We prove the contrapositive (@def-proof-by-contrapositive):
if $3 \mid n$, then $3 \mid n^2$.

Suppose $3 \mid n$.
Then $n = 3c$ for some integer $c$ (@def-divides), so

$$
\ba
n^2
&= (3c)^2
&& \text{(substitute } n = 3c \text{)}
\\&= 9 c^2
&& \text{(square each factor)}
\\&= 3 (3 c^2),
&& \text{(write } 9 = 3 \cd 3 \text{)}
\ea
$$

and $3 c^2$ is an integer (@rem-integer-closure), so $3 \mid n^2$.
By @thm-contrapositive, this proves the original proposition.

:::
